key_insight: SQD remains accurate even when the quantum sampling circuit is heavily simplified, allowing large reductions in non-Clifford and variational complexity before chemical-accuracy performance degrades.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper quantum chemistry workflows by compressing VQE-style circuits on qubit-reduced Hamiltonians, lowering simulation cost and hardware depth while preserving downstream SQD quality.
method: Gradient-based operator pruning removes low-impact excitation operators from the ansatz.
Clifford rounding snaps remaining parameters to nearby Clifford angles to reduce non-Clifford cost.
Both compressions are applied to VQE sampling circuits used for SQD subspace reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Across 21 molecules, median SQD error stayed within chemical accuracy at 50% compression on both pruning and rounding axes, with up to 33× simulation speedup and up to 2.8× transpiled-depth reduction on 6 IBM hardware targets without SQD accuracy loss.
watch_item: Compression is evaluated on specific molecules and ansätze, so performance may depend on the amount of ground-state overlap retained and may not generalize uniformly to harder chemistry instances.
paper_title: SQD-Enabled Circuit Compression for Resource-Efficient Quantum Chemistry
